correctness.rationale: With one cell per distinct ordered subsequence, signed deletion gives the integral cellular differential; the checked f-vector for n=5 is (5,20,48,41,10). Independent reconstruction verifies acyclicity of the oriented Hasse graph and all 60 unit cancellations, leaving a zero differential and critical dimensions 0,2,2,3. All 60 ordered pairs and all four ordered critical entries agree with the supplied JSON. The matching gives a Morse CW model with a single vertex and 2-skeleton S²∨S². In that model the only 3-to-2 boundary must be zero: the integral cancellation gives H3=Z and the 3-chain group is Z with no higher groups. Thus the 3-cell has zero degrees on both 2-cells, and by Hurewicz its attaching class in π2(S²∨S²) is zero. This proves the actual wedge, not just its Betti numbers. In n=2,3,4 the independent critical dimensions (0), (0,1), (0,2,2,2) give the stated point, circle, and three 2-spheres. Purity follows from generation by full words; nonzero homology below dimension four contradicts pure Boolean-cell shellability.
residual_risks: Integral and nonequivariant; no claim for n≥6 or for a different interpretation of word faces.

value.rationale: A single cycle type in the symmetric group is a canonical choice of generators, and topology of this subcomplex is not controlled by the full group or fixed-point complex. The low-order cutoff gives an exact test case in which a pure permutation-word complex has homology in two non-top degrees; the integral wedge identifies its topology more precisely than a rank calculation and is reusable as a benchmark for broader cycle-type families.
residual_risks: The scope is the initial segment of one natural family, not an all-n classification.
